gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each of its capacity tiers costs. Today's maker-store prices come to about $420–$560 per kWh from 1 kWh up to 11 kWh: $459 for 1 kWh (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic), $899 for 2 kWh (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2), $2,008 for 4 kWh, which covers ChatGPT's own 4.1 kWh example (DELTA 3 Max Plus plus its extra battery), $2,599 for 5.5 kWh (BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K) and $5,699 for 11 kWh (2× Apex 300 + 2× B300K + Hub A1).
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results (the results list is empty), so there were no cited rival pages to compare against. Its answer gives kWh tiers and a formula but no dollar figure for any tier and no product. It names Tesla Powerwall, EcoFlow and Jackery only as examples and gives no prices. A per-tier price ladder from the makers' own stores is new. It does not on its own decide a single pick, because the right product still depends on the shopper's load and how long they need it to run.
decides: It turns ChatGPT's sizing into a budget. The 'Wi-Fi, phones, lights' 1–2 kWh tier costs $459–$899. ChatGPT's 4.1 kWh fridge-plus-essentials estimate costs about $2,008 (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus plus a 2,048 Wh extra battery, 4,096 Wh). The '5–10 kWh essential home' tier starts at $2,599 for 5,529.6 Wh and 3,840 W (BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K, which is our product). The 10–20 kWh tier starts at $5,699 for 11,059.2 Wh and 7,680 W. Price per kWh hardly falls as you go bigger, so the pick should match the shopper's real need, not the bigger box. Per kWh, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($432/kWh) and Apex 300 + B300K ($470/kWh) undercut the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus ($561/kWh) and its expanded 4 kWh setup ($490/kWh).
